# `tracker` operations

The exact fields each `tracker.*` operation takes and returns.

<!-- Generated by `python scripts/codegen/docs_reference.py` from the op registry; edit the models, not this page. -->

Every op is `POST /v1/<op>` over HTTP and the MCP tool `loom_<op>`. The identity fields (`org`, `namespace`, `agent`, `user_id`, `session_id`) are filled from the token and the MCP session when a transport can; see [identities and namespaces](../../concepts/identities-and-namespaces.md). The [operations index](../operations.md) explains role, kind and the MCP `all` listing. Unknown input fields are served and named in `ignored_args`.

<!-- prettier-ignore-start -->

## `tracker.answer`

Answer a tracker question in prose — or from an artefact's anchors — by running the catalogue's templates: escalation / incident context, a customer across channels, incidents / escalations /…

`POST /v1/tracker.answer` · MCP `loom_tracker_answer` · role `viewer` · read · not listed under the MCP `all` toolset

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | `''` | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | required | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `question` | `str` | `''` | The question in prose; may be empty when `anchors` are given. |
| `anchors` | `dict[str, Any]` | *(computed)* | Structured anchors a client already holds: a PR's components and paths, an issue number and its frames, a customer, a version, a window, intent words — {numbers, number_kind, versions, components, paths, handles, customers, tests, terms… |
| `limit` | `int` | `10` | Rows per section, at most; the server caps it at 50. |
| `explain_only` | `bool` | `False` | Return the plan (sections marked `planned`) without reading the tracker. |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `intent` | `str` | What the planner read the question as (e.g. `release_readiness`); "" when unclear. |
| `anchors` | `dict[str, Any]` | The anchors the plan used: the prose's merged with the ones passed in. |
| `sections` | `list[dict[str, Any]]` | [{template, title, access, params, why, status served\|empty\|restricted_required\| tracker_unavailable\|planned, cites, rows}] |
| `searched` | `list[str]` | one string per section: template(params) — what was searched |
| `lines` | `list[str]` | Prose lines of the served sections with inline citations; empty with `explain_only`. |
| `restricted` | `bool` | True when the answering tracker namespace is restricted. |
| `verdict` | `str` | planned \| answered \| empty \| unknown (no anchor to plan on) |

## `tracker.binding`

What this namespace may ask the tracker plane: a QA namespace answers itself; a code namespace answers the tracker namespace bound to it (`LOOM_TRACKER_CODE_NAMESPACE_BINDINGS_JSON`), passed through…

`POST /v1/tracker.binding` · MCP `loom_tracker_binding` · role `viewer` · read · not listed under the MCP `all` toolset

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | `''` | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | required | The namespace the op reads or writes. |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tracker_namespace` | `str` | the namespace QA questions on the addressed namespace are answered by; "" when there is none the caller may read |
| `tracker_namespaces` | `list[str]` | Every tracker linked to the addressed code namespace the caller may read, primary (`tracker_namespace`) first; the searches read them all, a lookup by number reads the primary — or address another by name |
| `restricted` | `bool` | True when the answering tracker namespace is restricted. |
| `kind` | `str` | qa: the addressed namespace is a tracker namespace \| code: a code namespace bound to one the caller may read \| none: nothing to ask (unbound, refused, or neither — the three are one answer, so a refusal names nothing) |
| `authorized` | `bool` | True when the caller may ask a tracker here; False with `kind = none`. |
| `templates` | `list[str]` | catalogue template names the caller may run: public, plus the restricted class when `restricted` |

## `tracker.component`

One component's risk snapshot and its open issues, most severe first.

`POST /v1/tracker.component` · MCP `loom_tracker_component` · role `viewer` · read · not listed under the MCP `all` toolset

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | `''` | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | required | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `component` | `str` | required | Component name, matched exactly as the tracker spells it. |
| `limit` | `int` | `10` | At most this many open issues; the server caps it at 50. |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `component` | `str` | Echo of the requested component. |
| `risk` | `dict[str, Any]` | The component's latest risk snapshot row (columns as the source holds them); `{}` when none. |
| `open_issues` | `list[dict[str, Any]]` | Open issues in the component, most severe first: number, title, severity, labels, versions, bisect outcome, flaky/crash flags, url. |
| `known` | `bool` | True when the tracker has a risk row or an open issue for the component. |
| `tracker_unavailable` | `bool` | True when the source could not be read; the fields above are then empty, not a claim. |

## `tracker.contract`

The record contract as the register page shows it before anyone connects: every table loom reads, required or optional, each column's family, the type a view writes, whether a default is safe, what…

`POST /v1/tracker.contract` · MCP `loom_tracker_contract` · role `viewer` · read · not listed under the MCP `all` toolset

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | required | The org. |
| `database` | `str` | `'<database>'` | The database the templates name (default a placeholder). |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | `str` | The database name the templates use (the placeholder `<database>` when none valid was given). |
| `tables` | `list[dict[str, Any]]` | [{table, required, note, columns: [{name, family, type, must_map, note}]}] |
| `templates` | `dict[str, str]` | Table name -> a `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW` template with every column at its typed default. |

## `tracker.duplicate_check`

Does this draft already exist?

`POST /v1/tracker.duplicate_check` · MCP `loom_tracker_duplicate_check` · role `viewer` · read · not listed under the MCP `all` toolset

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | `''` | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | required | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `title` | `str` | `''` | The draft's title, as a reporter would file it. |
| `body` | `str` | `''` | The draft's body text. |
| `frames` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | qualified frames or raw trace lines, each at most 4,000 characters; normalised the way code.trace parses |
| `component` | `str` | `''` | The draft's component; boosts candidates with the same component. |
| `version` | `str` | `''` | The version the draft is about (`X.Y`, a longer one is cut to its minor); boosts candidates affecting it. |
| `mentions` | `list[int]` | *(computed)* | issue / PR numbers the draft refers to, beside the ones its text names |
| `paths` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | the finding's code-path evidence: repository paths a fix PR of a candidate may have touched (`fix_path`), and symbols matched like frames |
| `symbols` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | Code symbols from the finding, each at most 4,000 characters, matched like stack frames. |
| `issue_number` | `int` | `0` | the issue already filed for this draft (its own text is the query when title and body are empty; it is excluded; its recorded relations are read) |
| `top_k` | `int` | `10` | At most this many items; the server caps it at 50. |
| `as_of` | `str` | `''` | ISO 8601: only items created before it are candidates (replays); '' = now |
| `namespaces` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | The tracker namespaces to read (each a tracker namespace or a code namespace bound to one), the addressed one first; empty = every QA record the caller may read when addressed to a code namespace or the bound one, a single read when a… |
| `related_prs` | `bool` | `True` | Also search the PRs that may already address the draft (on none / related). loom_search's tracker leg turns it off: its 3 s budget has no room for the extra search |
| `rerank` | `bool` | `True` | Bisect's own check runs the legs alone — the rerank's LLM call does not fit the bisect's budget |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `verdict` | `str` | duplicate_of \| related \| none — `none` carries no items (file it) |
| `items` | `list[dict[str, Any]]` | [{kind, number, repo, url, title, state, state_reason, component, created_at, score, confidence (null when uncalibrated), relation: duplicate \| related, relation_recorded: duplicate_of \| related_to \| fixed_by \| none (the QA graph's edge… |
| `undecided` | `bool` | the top candidate sits in [related, duplicate) AND shares the component: route the list to a human |
| `epistemic` | `str` | calibrated (a stored fit scored the items) \| uncalibrated (no fit: `related` at most, confidence null) \| degraded (a leg, or one of several trackers, did not answer: a `none` is not clearance) \| unavailable (nobody read the record) |
| `thresholds` | `dict[str, float]` | {duplicate, related} — the served thresholds on the probability scale |
| `judge` | `dict[str, Any]` | The judge stage — ran, model, tokens, labels per candidate number, the numbers it promoted; absent when the stage is off |
| `fit_at` | `str` | When the stored calibration fit was computed; "" when no fit is stored. |
| `fit` | `dict[str, Any]` | {status served \| no_fit, fit_at, queries {n, positives, negatives}, auc, holdout_auc, tracker_namespace} |
| `query` | `dict[str, Any]` | what was searched: terms, frames and their source, mentions, component, versions, error_code, the wall, the legs' timings |
| `legs` | `dict[str, str]` | per leg: served \| empty \| skipped \| not_computed \| tracker_unavailable |
| `leg_status` | `list[TrackerLegStatus]` | Per leg of every namespace read: status ok \| degraded \| skipped, reason and message, retried, ms. |
| `tracker_unavailable` | `bool` | every leg failed to read: the verdict above is not a claim |
| `namespaces` | `list[str]` | The tracker namespaces this answer read (bound one first) and each one's own verdict / item count / epistemic / legs; every item in `items` names its `namespace`. |
| `by_namespace` | `dict[str, dict[str, Any]]` | Per namespace read: verdict, item count, epistemic, undecided, legs and `tracker_unavailable`. |
| `closest` | `list[dict[str, Any]]` | On `none` / `related`, up to three rows the fit scored under the related line whose title is near-identical to the draft's — [{namespace, kind, number, title, state, url, confidence, title_similarity, evidence}]; the verdict above stays… |
| `needs` | `list[dict[str, str]]` | the draft inputs the stored fit rewards and the draft left empty: [{input: body \| paths \| frames \| version \| component, what, feature}] |
| `closest_note` | `str` | one sentence: the same-titled record, why the fit did not call it, what to pass |
| `nearest` | `list[dict[str, Any]]` | On `none` / `related`, the fit's best scored-out issues that share a distinctive term with the draft, up to three rows shown in all (served items count) — [{namespace, number, title, state, url, confidence, why}]. |
| `rerank` | `dict[str, Any]` | The rerank stage — ran, model, prompt, pool size, picks [{number, label: same\|related, confidence}], tokens, ms, and the HyDE scan's own block; a pick leads `nearest` and never changes the verdict |
| `answer` | `str` | One sentence — already reported? fixed by which PR, in which release? or a PR that may already address it. |
| `related_prs` | `list[dict[str, Any]]` | On none / related, PRs that may already address the draft (code.pr_check) — [{number, title, state, relation, score, merged_at}] |

## `tracker.flaky`

Is this test a known flaky?

`POST /v1/tracker.flaky` · MCP `loom_tracker_flaky` · role `viewer` · read · not listed under the MCP `all` toolset

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | `''` | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | required | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `test_name` | `str` | required | The test to look up: flaky-test issues whose title holds every token of it match. |
| `limit` | `int` | `10` | At most this many issues; the server caps it at 50. |
| `include_signal` | `bool` | `False` | Also run `tracker.test_signal` on the test and return it in `signal`. |
| `window_days` | `int` | `0` | History window for `signal`, in days; 0 = the deployment default. |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `test_name` | `str` | The test name asked about, trimmed. |
| `known_flaky` | `bool` | True when at least one flaky-test issue names the test. |
| `open_issues` | `int` | How many of `issues` are still open. |
| `issues` | `list[dict[str, Any]]` | Matching flaky-test issues, newest first: number, title, state, labels, dates, url. |
| `verdict` | `str` | flaky_by_issue \| no_flaky_signal \| tracker_unavailable — the second is silence, not "not flaky"; the third is "nobody looked" |
| `tracker_unavailable` | `bool` | True when the source could not be read; `verdict` is then `tracker_unavailable`. |
| `signal` | `dict[str, Any] \| None` | The tracker.test_signal answer, only when asked for |

## `tracker.item`

The tracker record of up to ten issue / PR numbers: component, severity, bisect verdict and branches still affected, test presence, CI result, reviewers, backport lineage, and the fixes / backports…

`POST /v1/tracker.item` · MCP `loom_tracker_item` · role `viewer` · read · not listed under the MCP `all` toolset

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | `''` | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | required | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `numbers` | `list[int]` | required | Issue or PR numbers to read (1–10); duplicates fold and numbers <= 0 are dropped. |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `list[dict[str, Any]]` | One entry per known number: kind, state, title, author, dates, url, the tracker record (`tracker`), a one-line summary (`line`) and the files each `fixed_by` PR touched. |
| `unknown` | `list[int]` | numbers the tracker source has no row for — unknown, not absent (the upstream sync lags minutes) |
| `tracker_unavailable` | `bool` | the source could not be read (breaker open, budget exceeded, credential unset, kill switch): nothing above is a claim |

## `tracker.links`

Which PR probably fixed this issue — or which issue this PR probably fixed — when nobody wrote the link down.

`POST /v1/tracker.links` · MCP `loom_tracker_links` · role `viewer` · read · not listed under the MCP `all` toolset

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | `''` | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | required | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `issue_number` | `int` | `0` | The issue whose probable fixing PRs to list; wins over `pr_number`. 0 = none. |
| `pr_number` | `int` | `0` | The PR whose probably-fixed issues to list, when `issue_number` is 0. |
| `limit` | `int` | `10` | At most this many candidates; the server caps it at 50. |
| `include_record` | `bool` | `True` | Also read the tracker graph's `fixes` edges live and mark candidates it confirms. |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `subject` | `dict[str, Any]` | {kind: issue \| pr, number} |
| `verdict` | `str` | candidates \| none \| not_computed — none: a list was computed and holds no row above the floor (never "no fix exists"); not_computed: the pass has not covered this number (outside its window, or never ran) |
| `items` | `list[dict[str, Any]]` | [{issue_number, pr_number, rank, score, why: [closes\|mentions, lexical, frames, component], features {bm25_title, bm25_body, bm25_norm, window_hours, component_match, frames_symbols, frames_files, frames_total, closes_mention}, terms… |
| `epistemic` | `str` | Always `candidate`: these are computed guesses, not recorded links. |
| `record` | `dict[str, Any]` | the tracker graph's fixes edges for the subject: {status served \| empty \| skipped \| tracker_unavailable, numbers: [...]} |
| `computed_at` | `str` | the table's last write for this namespace (what `not_computed` is relative to) |
| `tracker_unavailable` | `bool` | the record leg could not be read; the candidates above still stand |

## `tracker.release`

Release readiness for one version (`26.3`): the blocker rows with their status and the latest health snapshot.

`POST /v1/tracker.release` · MCP `loom_tracker_release` · role `viewer` · read · not listed under the MCP `all` toolset

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | `''` | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | required | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `version` | `str` | required | The release to check, as the tracker names it (e.g. `26.3`). |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | `str` | Echo of the requested version. |
| `blockers` | `list[dict[str, Any]]` | The release's rows: `ref`, `status`, `issue_state`, `fix_version` and `active` (an open `Blockers` row); active ones first. |
| `active_blockers` | `int` | How many of `blockers` are active (status `Blockers` and the issue still open). |
| `health` | `dict[str, Any]` | Latest health snapshot: `open_blockers`, `critical_untested`, `total_items`, `snapshot_date`; `{}` when none. |
| `tracker_unavailable` | `bool` | True when the source could not be read; the lists above are then empty, not a claim. |

## `tracker.similar`

The reports that already say it: duplicate and related issues / PRs for a pasted report (`text`), an existing item (`issue_number` — its own title, body, component, versions and error code become…

`POST /v1/tracker.similar` · MCP `loom_tracker_similar` · role `viewer` · read · not listed under the MCP `all` toolset

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | `''` | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | required | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `text` | `str` | `''` | A pasted report to search for; may be empty when `issue_number` or `frames` is given. |
| `issue_number` | `int` | `0` | An existing item whose own text is the query; only older items are candidates. 0 = none. |
| `frames` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | qualified frames or raw trace lines, each at most 4,000 characters; normalised the way code.trace parses |
| `kinds` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | issue \| pr \| incident (incidents only through a restricted tracker namespace) |
| `top_k` | `int` | `10` | At most this many items; the server caps it at 50. |
| `legs` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | the legs to run — lexical, fields, frames, mentions, vector; the default is all (the bench arms one at a time; `fields` are the equality boosts on the lexical leg and run only with it; `mentions` are the items the text names by number) |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `list[dict[str, Any]]` | [{kind, number, title, state, state_reason, score, why: [lexical\|frames\| mentions\|vector, component, version, error_code, duplicate_of\| related_to\|fixed_by], relation: duplicate_of\|related_to\|fixed_by\|none (what the tracker graph records… |
| `query` | `dict[str, Any]` | what was searched: the query item (number, kind, known), the selected terms, the frames and where they came from (caller \| body), the wall; with the vector leg: `fresh_items` (items changed upstream since the pass's cursor, embedded on… |
| `legs` | `dict[str, str]` | per leg: served \| empty \| skipped \| restricted_required \| zero_embedding \| not_computed \| tracker_unavailable — a leg that did not run is named, never silent (not_computed: the vector table holds no row for the namespace — the… |
| `epistemic` | `str` | Always `lower_bound`: a miss does not prove no similar report exists. |
| `tracker_unavailable` | `bool` | every leg failed to read: nothing above is a claim |
| `namespaces` | `list[str]` | The trackers searched, primary first, when the addressed repository links more than one (each item then names its `namespace`) |

## `tracker.source.add`

Register a tracker source: a ClickHouse endpoint and database holding the record contract (docs/features/tracker/record-contract.md), a read-only credential, and the tracker namespaces that read it.

`POST /v1/tracker.source.add` · MCP `loom_tracker_source_add` · role `viewer` · write · audited · not listed under the MCP `all` toolset

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | required | The org registering the source. |
| `name` | `str` | required | Source name: 2–32 lower-case letters, digits, - or _. |
| `host` | `str` | required | ClickHouse host (a URL is accepted; only the host is kept). |
| `port` | `int` | `8443` | HTTPS port (8443 on ClickHouse Cloud). |
| `secure` | `bool` | `True` | TLS. |
| `database` | `str` | required | The database holding the contract views. |
| `user` | `str` | required | A READ-ONLY user (SELECT on the views and system.columns). |
| `password` | `str` | required | Stored encrypted at rest; never returned. |
| `namespaces` | `list[TrackerSourceNamespaceSpec]` | required | The tracker namespaces reading this source. |
| `mapping` | `dict[str, Any] \| None` | `None` | Per logical table (github_issues, github_prs, edges, …): the team's table (`source`) and, per logical column, an expression over its columns — a column name, {lit}, {concat}, {coalesce}, {eq}, {in}, {has}, {cast}, {lower}. |
| `dry_run` | `bool` | `False` | Run every check and write nothing; a schema that fails the contract is returned with view_templates instead of refused. |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `str` | The registered source's name, normalised. |
| `host` | `str` | The stored host (only the host part of a URL). |
| `database` | `str` | The database the source reads. |
| `namespaces` | `list[dict[str, Any]]` | [{namespace, repos, classification, join_policy}] |
| `contract` | `dict[str, Any]` | The record-contract report (`ok`, missing tables and columns, type mismatches, …). |
| `roles` | `list[str]` | Roles the credential holds; the read-only check reads their grants too. |
| `my_role` | `str` | `admin` when the caller becomes the namespaces' first admin; "" with auth off. |
| `dry_run` | `bool` | A dry run says what it would write and writes nothing; view_templates = table → a CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW draft for each required table the schema fails on ({} when it meets the contract) |
| `written` | `bool` | True when the source and its namespaces were stored; False on a dry run. |
| `view_templates` | `dict[str, str]` | On a dry run: table -> a view draft for each required table the schema fails; `{}` when it meets the contract or a `mapping` was given. |

## `tracker.source.check`

Run the record-contract check on a configured tracker source now: the same read the boot gate runs, its verdict cached.

`POST /v1/tracker.source.check` · MCP `loom_tracker_source_check` · role `viewer` · read · not listed under the MCP `all` toolset

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | required | The org. |
| `name` | `str` | required | The source name. |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `str` | The source checked, normalised. |
| `database` | `str` | The database the source reads. |
| `reachable` | `bool` | False when the contract read failed or took over 8 s; `contract` then says why. |
| `contract` | `dict[str, Any]` | The record-contract report; `{ok: None, summary}` when unreachable. |
| `view_templates` | `dict[str, str]` | The view drafts for each required table the schema fails on |

## `tracker.source.inspect`

Connect with a read-only credential and say what the database holds — every table the user can read, its columns and types — plus a first mapping of it onto loom's logical model.

`POST /v1/tracker.source.inspect` · MCP `loom_tracker_source_inspect` · role `viewer` · read · not listed under the MCP `all` toolset

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | required | The org. |
| `name` | `str` | `''` | A registered tracker to inspect with its own credential. |
| `host` | `str` | `''` | ClickHouse host (a URL is accepted). |
| `port` | `int` | `8443` | HTTPS port of the ClickHouse endpoint (8443 on ClickHouse Cloud); ignored with `name`. |
| `secure` | `bool` | `True` | Connect over TLS; ignored with `name`. |
| `database` | `str` | `''` | The database to inspect. |
| `user` | `str` | `''` | A read-only user. |
| `password` | `str` | `''` | Never stored by inspect. |
| `repos` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | The repositories the tracker holds (Org/repo); one lets a table without a repository column still build 'Org/repo#number' references. |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `host` | `str` | The host inspected (only the host part of a URL). |
| `database` | `str` | The database inspected. |
| `tables` | `list[dict[str, Any]]` | [{table, engine, rows, columns: [{name, type}]}] |
| `roles` | `list[str]` | Roles the credential holds; the read-only check reads their grants too. |
| `proposal` | `dict[str, Any]` | {mode: views\|mapping, roles: {logical: table}, fields: {logical: {column: {from, confidence}}}, mapping: mapping.SourceMapping JSON \| None} |

## `tracker.source.list`

The tracker sources of an org: every configured source with its contract verdict, breaker and freshness, and the tracker namespaces reading it — each with the directory row's effective join rule and…

`POST /v1/tracker.source.list` · MCP `loom_tracker_source_list` · role `viewer` · read · not listed under the MCP `all` toolset

## `tracker.test_signal`

Flaky, regression or infrastructure?

`POST /v1/tracker.test_signal` · MCP `loom_tracker_test_signal` · role `viewer` · read · not listed under the MCP `all` toolset

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | `''` | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | required | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `test_name` | `str` | required | The test to read, as CI names it; an unknown name answers `unknown_test` with the tests it matches. |
| `window_days` | `int` | `0` | History window in days; 0 = the deployment default. |
| `code_namespace` | `str` | `''` | Code namespace whose PR ledger churn and smells are read from; "" = the deployment's; the caller needs read access to it. |
| `include_churn` | `bool` | `True` | Read the churn of the test's home file(s) and mapped sources; False skips it. |
| `pr_number` | `int` | `0` | The PR head whose previous-outcome streak is read (0 = none) |
| `include_smells` | `bool` | `True` | The static smell flags from the test's own source chunks |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `test_name` | `str` | The test the answer is for, trimmed (the matched test when `resolved_from` is set). |
| `verdict` | `str` | flaky \| regression_candidate \| infra_candidate \| no_signal \| unknown_test \| tracker_unavailable — no_signal is silence, not health; unknown_test is a name no test carries, with the tests it matches |
| `why` | `list[str]` | Plain sentences giving the reasons for `verdict`. |
| `lower_bound` | `float` | Wilson 95 % lower bound of the failure rate over the window's runs: the least the test can plausibly fail; small n → small bound |
| `window_days` | `int` | The window actually read, in days (the default when 0 was asked). |
| `since` | `str` | Start of the window, ISO UTC (hour-truncated). |
| `features` | `dict[str, Any]` | runs, fails, fail_rate, flips, steps, flip_rate, entropy, rerun_flips, prs, failing_prs, branch_fails, last_true_fail(+_head), last_fail_at, first_run_at, fail_hours |
| `infra` | `dict[str, Any]` | {k, min_prs, storm_hours, hours, share, available} |
| `churn` | `dict[str, Any]` | {available, days, home_paths, home_prs, home_recent, source_paths, source_prs, source_recent, code_namespace \| reason} |
| `thresholds` | `dict[str, Any]` | The deployment thresholds the verdict used (min runs, flip rate, co-failure knobs). |
| `source` | `str` | where the history came from: the checks source clause without its credentials |
| `timings_ms` | `dict[str, int]` | Milliseconds spent per leg (`history`, `co_failures`, `churn`, `smells`, …). |
| `tracker_unavailable` | `bool` | True when the history could not be read, or an unread leg decides the verdict; `verdict` is then `tracker_unavailable`. |
| `rollup` | `dict[str, Any]` | What the daily roll-up covered of the window {available, days, from, to, live_since, missing_days, partial_day \| reason} |
| `streak` | `dict[str, Any]` | The previous-outcome streak of (pr_number, test) — {pr_number, known, fail_days, last_fail_day, fails_on_day, tail_streak, last_outcome, subsequent_failure, source} |
| `smells` | `dict[str, Any]` | Flaky-test smell tokens counted over the test's source {available, loc, counts, flags \| reason} |
| `prior` | `dict[str, Any]` | {next_run_on_pr, flake_indicators, flake_prior} |
| `unavailable_reason` | `str` | Why the source could not be read; "" when it was. |
| `candidates` | `list[dict[str, Any]]` | On `unknown_test`, the rolled tests whose names start with (else contain) the asked one, most runs first — [{test_name, runs, fails}] — and how many match in all; never summed into one test's features |
| `candidate_matches` | `int` | On `unknown_test`: how many rolled tests match the name in all. |
| `resolved_from` | `str` | The asked name when the answer is for the only test it matched |
